title: After an etale neighbourhood the points of an unramified fibre separate into closed pieces
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for an unramified map and a prime of the base there is an etale neighbourhood over which the base change splits into factors that are surjective over the neighbourhood, each with a single prime over the point, together with a factor having no prime over it (statement lines 42218-42241). The proof invokes the etale splitting of a quasi-finite map to get the product decomposition with finite factors, then shows each finite factor becomes a surjection after inverting one element of the base and verifies the listed properties (proof lines 42243-42268). Turning the local surjectivity of a finite map into a global one by inverting an element is the step that carries the argument. H2.
